title: ChatGPT Computer History Creates New Attack Surface for macOS Infostealers
content_md: OpenAI’s new ChatGPT Computer History feature for macOS is designed to make AI assistance more context-aware, but its local “diary” of user activity may also create a high-value target for macOS infostealers . Released for the ChatGPT macOS desktop app, Computer History is disabled by default and currently applies to ChatGPT Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. The opt-in capability converts selected activity across apps and websites into searchable memories that ChatGPT and Codex can use in later conversations. ChatGPT Computer History Creates New Attack Surface The feature requires ChatGPT Memories to be enabled, while Business and Enterprise users need workspace-level administrative approval to activate it individually. Unlike Microsoft Recall’s original screenshot-centric model, Computer History relies on macOS Accessibility APIs to record interaction events. The feature can collect typed text, clicks, keyboard shortcuts, application switches, window titles, and other interface activity from selected apps and sites. OpenAI says it does not capture screenshots, screen recordings, microphone input, system audio, or activity in private browsing windows. The security concern lies in how this data is transformed and stored. Raw interaction events are retained locally for up to 48 hours while hidden background sessions summarize them into contextual records.
